title: CAP: when the link breaks, pick a side
intro: Two nodes must agree on the last concert ticket. Then the network between them breaks. What now?

predict.question: During a network partition, can a system be fully consistent AND fully available?
options: Yes, if you add a third node
predict.reveal: A partition means a node cannot confirm with the other side. It either refuses requests (consistent) or answers anyway and may diverge (available).

takeaway: CAP: when a partition happens you choose consistency (refuse some requests) or availability (answer, maybe wrongly).

steps.say: Node A and Node B each keep a copy of the data: 1 ticket left. They sync every change to each other.
A network partition: the cable between A and B is cut. Both nodes are alive but cannot talk to each other.
Path 1, choose Consistency. A buyer asks Node A for the last ticket.
Node A cannot tell B about the sale. If it sells anyway, B might sell it too.
So A refuses: an error, but the data stays correct. We kept consistency and lost availability.
Rewind. Path 2, choose Availability. Same partition, same buyer, same last ticket.
Node A just answers: sold. It cannot tell B, so B still thinks 1 ticket is left.
Meanwhile a second buyer reaches Node B and asks for the same ticket.
B also says yes. Both buyers are happy, but the copies now disagree.
When the link heals, the nodes find one ticket sold twice and must reconcile, maybe refunding someone.
Partitions will happen, so real systems choose: banks lean consistent, social feeds lean available.
